newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close off a hair on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close off a hair on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed modest early gains to slightly close down on profit-taking, traders and analysts said.

"What we saw today was just light profit-taking, which was to be expected after yesterday's speculative gains ahead of falls in primary rates," said Roberto Galvan, analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 2.61 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,268.84. Volume was regular at 71.6 million shares traded.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 29.08 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, 77 basis points down from last week. Traders said this was expected as the central bank had relaxed its daily liquidity objective.
Galvn said the bourse continued to be sluggish due to investors preferring to invest in New York and waiting for the peso to weaken and magnify peso returns.
On the broad market, 110 stocks were traded, of which losers outnumbered winners 46 to 37.
Notable gainers in volume terms were autoparts maker Iasasa and mining firm Grupo Mexico.
Traders said that Iasasa stock gained -- closing up four centavos at 37 -- on bargain-hunting after a debt restructuring plan for the firm was announced on Tuesday.
"GMexico traded strongly, and was in great demand, probably due to its involvement in railroad privatization bidding," said a trader. GMexico ended up 1.25 pesos at 26.05 pesos.

Publishers GFesa, followed by construction firm Tribasa, headed the losers list. They ended down nine and 60 centavos, respectively, at 1.66 and 20.10 pesos. Traders said these two companies had gloomy year-end outlooks.
Dealers said they expected a very quiet session on Thursday, as U.S. markets will be closed for Thanksgiving.
The Mexican stock market will be open on Thursday, but there will be no open outcry.
